config.subtitle: Quick answers about the BerlinWalk free walking tour.

items.q: How long is the BerlinWalk free walking tour?
items.a: The tour is approximately **3 km long and takes about 2 hours**. The route is flat and easy — no rushing. Every stop has time for photos, questions, and a bit of breathing room before the next part of the city.

items.q: Where does the walking tour start and end?
items.a: We start at the **World Clock (Weltzeituhr) on Alexanderplatz** — the rotating globe sculpture in the middle of the square, easy to find. The tour ends at **Hackescher Markt**, one of Berlin's most charming neighborhoods — perfect for food and drinks afterwards.

items.q: Is the BerlinWalk tour really free?
items.a: **The walk is tip-based, with no fixed tour price.** Booking requires a €2 refundable deposit per guest. We refund it after confirmed attendance or cancellation at least 24 hours before; late cancellations and no-shows are not refunded. Your tip at the end is separate and up to you.

items.q: What will I see on the 12-stop walking tour?
items.a: The route covers **800 years of Berlin history** through the city's oldest quarter — Alexanderplatz, the World Clock, the TV Tower (and the famous "Pope's Revenge"), the Hohenzollern Crypt beneath the Berliner Dom, UNESCO Museum Island, and Berlin's hidden medieval neighborhood. Most other Berlin tours skip this part of the city entirely.

items.q: Do I need to book the walking tour in advance?
items.a: **Yes — please book online** so we can plan group sizes. Booking on **berlinwalk.com** requires a €2 refundable deposit per guest. Walk-ups are welcome only if there's space, but on busy days the tour can fill up.
